declarations.documentation:
One model step over the conversation + tool schemas — THE provider seam. A provider module serves
this request for the extent of a continuation (`use gemini.provider(...)`), so the loop stays
provider-agnostic and providers stay loop-agnostic.
declarations.name: infer_step
declarations.signature: request infer_step(history: array[types.message], tool_metas: array[reflection.agent_metadata]) -> types.step

declarations.documentation: Infer a single reply with no tools (the common chat case).
declarations.name: reply

declarations.checkedType: agent(image: file) -> file
declarations.documentation:
Tool: load an image file into your visual context. Pass the file's handle object — a bare
{"$ref": "<id>"} suffices (copy the id from the conversation); the image content arrives with
this tool's result, so you can see it on your next step.
declarations.name: view_image

declarations.checkedType: agent(history: array[call_turn | result_turn | turn], max_steps: integer, tools: array[agent(...never) -> unknown with E0]) -> string with infer_step | throw[decode_error | call_error] | E0
declarations.documentation:
Run the tool-using model loop, generic over the tools' shared effect @E@: derive each tool's schema
with `reflection.get_metadata`, then up to @max_steps@ times perform `infer_step` against the ambient
provider; on a batch of tool calls, dispatch them all CONCURRENTLY with `parallel for` (each resolves
its tool by name and invokes it by value via `reflection.call_agent`, validating the model's args
against the tool's schema), then feed every result back as a new turn; on a final answer, return it.
declarations.name: infer_with_tools
declarations.signature: agent infer_with_tools[effect E](history: array[types.message], tools: array[agent never -> unknown with E], max_steps: integer) -> string

declarations.documentation:
The outcome of decoding a model's raw tool args: the decoded value, or the decode error rendered
readable (fed back to the model as the tool's error result, so it corrects on the next step).
declarations.name: decoded

declarations.documentation: See @decoded@ — the failure half (a malformed replayed file handle is the observed case).
declarations.name: decode_failed

declarations.checkedType: agent(args: json_array | json_boolean | json_integer | json_null | json_number | json_object | json_string) -> (decode_failed | decoded)
declarations.documentation:
Decode a model's raw args to a plain value, catching the decode error locally (its effect row is
concrete here — a catch inside the generically-effectful dispatch would also capture the TOOLS' own
typed throws, which the checker rightly rejects).
declarations.name: decode_args

declarations.checkedType: agent(call: tool_call, tools: array[agent(...never) -> unknown with E1]) -> tool_result with throw[decode_error | call_error] | E1
declarations.documentation:
Find the tool whose metadata name is the model's pick and invoke it by value via
`reflection.call_agent` (the model's args decode to a plain value, and the delegation boundary
validates them against the tool's schema — the compiled signature of a Katari agent, or the
server-declared schema of an MCP tool). A hallucinated name, undecodable args, or a panicking tool
is fed back as an error result so the model corrects on the next step. The result's `file` values
are collected off its wire form so the provider can show them to the model (their `$ref` handles are
already visible in the result text).
declarations.name: dispatch_one
declarations.signature: agent dispatch_one[effect E](tools: array[agent never -> unknown with E], call: types.tool_call) -> types.tool_result

declarations.checkedType: agent(node: json_array | json_boolean | json_integer | json_null | json_number | json_object | json_string) -> array[file] with throw[decode_error]
declarations.documentation:
Collect every `file` value out of a tool result's wire form: in encoded json a file is its `$ref`
handle object (`json.decode[file]` revives it), so a generated image is found wherever the tool put
it — a bare return, the MCP bridge's { text, files }, or nested structure.
declarations.name: collect_result_files
declarations.signature: agent collect_result_files(node: json.json) -> array[file] with prelude.throw[json.decode_error]

declarations.checkedType: agent(entries: record[json_array | json_boolean | json_integer | json_null | json_number | json_object | json_string]) -> boolean
declarations.documentation:
Whether an encoded object is a `file`'s handle: it carries `$ref` AND its semantic kind is
"file" — a blob-backed *string* also encodes to a `$ref` handle, and must not revive as a file.
declarations.name: is_file_handle

declarations.checkedType: agent(node: json_array | json_boolean | json_integer | json_null | json_number | json_object | json_string) -> unknown
declarations.documentation:
Flatten a LITERAL `json` document into the plain value it denotes: a `json_object` becomes a record
with the SAME keys, a `json_array` an array, each scalar itself — no key is ever reinterpreted. This
is the sound way to splice a parsed-json subtree (a tool's JSON Schema from `get_metadata`, a model's
replayed tool_call args) into an `http.json` value-tree body, where a `file` rides as an actual file
value: `json.decode[unknown]` would instead read the subtree through the value-wire codec, mistaking a
schema's literal `$ref` / `$defs` / `$constructor` key for a file handle or discriminator and
corrupting it. (This differs from the loop's `decode_args`, which DELIBERATELY takes the wire reading:
a model's `$ref` argument SHOULD revive as a file to pass to a tool — here we echo the document back
verbatim instead.) On the wire the record's `$`-keys are re-escaped and the `http.json` materialiser
un-escapes them, so the server receives the original keys.
declarations.name: json_to_value
declarations.signature: agent json_to_value(node: json.json) -> unknown with pure

declarations.documentation:
A deterministic two-way mapping between a tool's real (qualified) name and the shortened name a
provider sends on the wire. @real_to_wire@ is keyed by the qualified name (used when encoding a tool
declaration or replaying a call turn), @wire_to_real@ by the wire name (used to reverse the model's
pick); both are total over one step's tools — see @build_name_map@.
declarations.name: name_map

declarations.checkedType: agent(name: string) -> string
declarations.documentation:
Fold a wire name onto a qualified name: every character outside a provider's `[a-zA-Z0-9_-]` name
alphabet (the dot of a qualified name, above all) folds to `_`, then the result is capped at the
providers' 64-character limit.
declarations.name: sanitize_name

declarations.checkedType: agent(base: string, index: integer) -> string
declarations.documentation:
Disambiguate a colliding wire name with an ordinal suffix (`_2`, `_3`, …), reserving room so the
result still fits the 64-character cap.
declarations.name: suffixed_name
declarations.signature: agent suffixed_name(base: string, index: integer) -> string

declarations.checkedType: agent(real: string, taken: record[string]) -> string
declarations.documentation:
Choose a free wire name for @real@ given the wire names already @taken@: its sanitized form, or —
when sanitizing collapsed two distinct qualified names onto one token, or truncation shared a prefix —
the first free ordinal-suffixed form. The suffix is decided by @taken@'s size (processing order), so
the choice is deterministic.
declarations.name: assign_wire_name

parameters.documentation: The wire names already assigned this step.
parameters.label: taken

taken.description: The wire names already assigned this step.

declarations.signature: agent assign_wire_name(taken: record[string], real: string) -> string

declarations.checkedType: agent(tool_metas: array[agent_metadata]) -> name_map
declarations.documentation:
Build the deterministic wire-name @name_map@ for one step's tools. Walking @tool_metas@ in order,
each tool's qualified name is assigned a free wire name against the names already placed, so the same
tool list always yields the same map — which is why the map needs no durable state (see the section
note). A provider whose wire vocabulary admits the qualified name (Gemini) never calls this.
declarations.name: build_name_map

declarations.checkedType: agent(map: name_map, real: string) -> string
declarations.documentation:
The wire name for a qualified tool name — used to encode a tool declaration and to re-encode a
replayed call turn. Falls back to the qualified name for a tool absent from the map (never happens for
a map built from the same step's tools).
declarations.name: wire_name_of
declarations.signature: agent wire_name_of(map: name_map, real: string) -> string

declarations.checkedType: agent(map: name_map, wire: string) -> string
declarations.documentation:
The qualified tool name for a wire name — used to reverse the model's pick so the loop dispatches by
the real name. Falls back to the wire name itself for an unknown name (a hallucinated tool), which the
loop then reports as an unknown tool.
declarations.name: real_name_of

parameters.documentation: The wire name the model returned.
parameters.label: wire

wire.description: The wire name the model returned.

declarations.signature: agent real_name_of(map: name_map, wire: string) -> string

a handle note.
declarations.name: anthropic_is_image

declarations.checkedType: agent(text: string) -> unknown
declarations.documentation:
A text content block — `{ "type": "text", "text": @text@ }`, built as a raw value tree. `type`
is a keyword, so the object is assembled with `record.set` instead of a literal.
declarations.name: anthropic_text_block

declarations.checkedType: agent(attachment: file) -> unknown
declarations.documentation:
An image content block: a base64 `source` whose `media_type` is the file's recorded type and whose
`data` slot holds the file VALUE placed DIRECTLY into the tree. `http.json` materialises that slot —
reading the bytes and base64-ing them in place — only at the send boundary, so the image content never
rides the value plane, the durable call record or the trace. `type` / `data` are keywords, so those
slots are assembled with `record.set`.
declarations.name: anthropic_image_block

declarations.checkedType: agent(files: array[file], text: string) -> unknown
declarations.documentation:
A turn's content: the plain string (text + every file's handle note) when the turn carries no image,
or an array of one text block plus one image block per image file when it does. An image file inlines
so the model can SEE it; a non-image file stays a handle note (the image block takes only images). The
text block still carries every file's handle note, so the model can replay any of them into a tool.
declarations.name: anthropic_turn_content

declarations.documentation:
One turn in a conversation: who spoke ("user" / "model"), what they said, and any files attached
to it (a Discord attachment, a generated image). Files ride as blob handles; each provider decides
when to inline their content for the model (see the providers' inline policy).
declarations.name: turn
declarations.signature: data turn(role: string, text: string, files: array[file])

declarations.documentation:
One tool the model wants to invoke this step — @name@ is its function name (the dispatch key and
the model-facing call/response record), @opaque@ is any provider token that must be replayed
verbatim on the call turn (Gemini's thought signature, OpenAI's call id), @args@ is the model's
argument object as parsed json (replayed verbatim; `json.decode[unknown]` turns it into the plain
value `reflection.call_agent` dispatches with).
declarations.name: tool_call
declarations.signature: data tool_call(name: string, opaque: string, args: json.json)

declarations.documentation:
A tool's output for the model, keyed by the tool @name@ / @call_id@ so it round-trips as a function
response. @files@ are the `file` values found in the result (a screenshot an MCP tool returned, an
edited image): @text@ already shows their `$ref` handles (the result's wire form), and the provider
additionally inlines their content for the model while the result is fresh.
declarations.name: tool_result
declarations.signature: data tool_result(name: string, call_id: string, text: string, files: array[file])

declarations.documentation: A conversation turn recording the model's tool-call batch — replayed so the next step shows the model what it already asked for.
declarations.name: call_turn

declarations.documentation: A conversation turn carrying the results of a tool-call batch.
declarations.name: result_turn

declarations.documentation: One inference step's decision: a final reply text for the user.
declarations.name: step_final

declarations.documentation: One inference step's decision: invoke a batch of tools (dispatched in parallel, results fed back together).
declarations.name: step_call
